content.title: Chuck Norris, film star and martial artist, dies aged 86
content.text: Actor and martial artist Chuck Norris, known for his roles in The Way Of The Dragon and Missing In Action, has died after a sudden hospitalisation.The Hollywood star was aged 86.In a statement, his family said they shared the news of his death with "heavy hearts"."To the world, he was a martial artist, actor, and a symbol of strength," the family posted on Instagram."To us, he was a devoted husband, a loving father and grandfather, an incredible brother, and the heart of our family."He lived his life with faith, purpose, and an unwavering commitment to the people he loved. "Through his work, discipline, and kindness, he inspired millions around the world and left a lasting impact on so many lives."Norris fell ill and was hospitalised in Hawaii on Thursday for an undisclosed condition.Chuck Norris has died at the age of 86. (Reuters: Troy Taormina )In the statement, the family said it would like to keep the details of his passing private, adding "please know that he was surrounded by his family and was at peace". The actor celebrated his 86th birthday this month, marking the event with a video of him boxing on social media.The video was accompanied with the caption: "I don't age. I level up.""Nothing like some playful action on a sunny day to make you feel young," he added.Norris was a karate champion before a film starNorris was born Carlos Ray Norris in Oklahoma on March 19, 1940.At the age of 12, he moved to California with his family and later joined the US Air Force.It was during a deployment to Korea that he started training in martial arts.Actor Chuck Norris, left, shakes hands with Gunnery Sgt John C Pollack in Iraq in November 2006. (US Marine Corps)He went on to become a six-time undefeated World Professional Middleweight Karate champion. He also founded his own Korean-based American hard style of karate, known sometimes as Chun Kuk Do, which has awarded more than 3,300 Chuck Norris System black belts worldwide. But in 1962, Norris was honourably discharged from the force.He applied to become a police officer but was put on a waitlist.That is when the martial arts expert turned to acting, with his debut film The Wrecking Crew in 1968.Actors actors Bruce Lee (R) and Chuck Norris during the filming of The Way of the Dragon. (AFP)Four years later, his epic fight with the kung fu superstar Bruce Lee in The Way of The Dragon helped turn Norris into an icon on the big and small screen.He went on to act in more than 20 movies, such as Missing in Action, The Delta Force, and Sidekicks.Norris also made a surprise comedic appearance as a decisive judge in the final match of the 2004 movie Dodgeball.In more recent years, Norris has become a viral sensation online, embracing the meme craze.Chuck Norris speaking at a National Rifle Association meeting. (Reuters: Chris Keane)Dolph Lundgren, who worked with Norris on The Expendables 2, said the star was a "role model"."Chuck Norris is a champ," he wrote in a tribute on Instagram."Someone who had the respect, humility and strength it takes to be a man."We will miss you, my friend."Sylvester Stallone, another Expendables 2 co-star, remembered Norris as a "great man".“I had a great time working with Chuck," the actor wrote in a tribute."He was All American in every way."Jean-Claude Van Damme said he had always respected his friend Norris."He will never be forgotten," the martial artist and actor wrote.Actor Chuck Norris in 2010. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)Norris's son, Dakota, said he would remember his father for his generosity, kindness, strength and discipline."You lived your life with purpose and with love for all people," he wrote in a tribute on Instagram."The memories we made, the lessons you taught me and the constant laughs we shared will stay with me for the rest of my life."His granddaughter, Greta Norris, also remembered him as "one of the most special" and an "icon"."You all knew Chuck Norris as the man who counted to infinity twice, the man who got bit by a cobra and the cobra died," she wrote in her post."I knew him as the old man who would come to grandparents' days at school, my soccer games, and cheer me on as proud as he could be."
